changes.old: The corrected omega_n=(psi_{n+2}psi_{n-1}^2-psi_{n-2}psi_{n+1}^2)/(4y) and the even recurrence give psi_{2n}=2psi_n omega_n; n=1,2 follow from the bases. Therefore 2y([n]P)psi_n(P)^4=psi_{2n}(P), while x([n]P)psi_n(P)^2=phi_n(P). For a nonidentity point P in the torsion-free carrier and n!=0, [n]P is not the identity, so psi_n(P)!=0 by the scalar-coordinate theorem and coprimality. With this guard, the two cleared equations uniquely recover both coordinates of [n]P. The inverse-norm guard is the separately supplied field encoding of nonzero elements of K0; it is not established by division polynomials. n=0 and identity P use their explicit identity branches. Negative n uses psi_{-n}=-psi_n and group negation, preserving the ordinate sign. This supplies current278–304 and its actual scalar-template use. The inaccessible Silverman errata are not a premise: closure-batch-010 supersedes the earlier A056 source-retrieval gap with the pinned Sutherland source. Existing finite scalar tests are supplementary checks, not the proof.

Therefore 2y([n]P)psi_n(P)^4=psi_{2n}(P), while x([n]P)psi_n(P)^2=phi_n(P). changes.old: Milne, Class Field Theory v4.03 (6August2020), ChapterV Theorem2.2, printed p.155: for every positive integer modulus m and every a coprime to m the rational primes congruent to a modulo m have Dirichlet density 1/phi(m), hence infinitely many. Exact PDF SHA256 50d79af78250a9f1117ad9d337e0b231704a533fc707966ed1bfa52e13d498f5; this is an author course note. In current306–308 set the fixed positive integer W=4 product_{p<=324}p. There are finitely many unit classes a modulo W. Each has infinitely many primes, and deleting the finite set <=324 leaves infinitely many. Ascending enumeration with finite trial primality tests and a congruence test therefore stops after finding22 in each class. The union is a fixed finite catalogue H_cat; its product with product_{p<=324}p defines N_s. This proves termination of this particular catalogue only, with no effective bound on its final prime and no claim about every later prime choice. The successful M0 index and its proof are separate.
changes.new: For every fixed integer q>=3 and gcd(a,q)=1, the published Bennett–Martin–O'Bryant–Rechnitzer estimate gives theta(x;q,a)=x/phi(q)+O_q(x/log x). The exact source and the deduction of infinitude are supplied in ../prime-realization-current/SOURCE.md, lines3–4. In current306–308 the fixed integer W=4 product_{p<=324}p is at least4, so this estimate applies to every unit class modulo W. Choosing log x greater than twice the fixed implied constant times phi(W) makes theta(x;W,a) at least x/(2phi(W)), which is unbounded. Thus each such class contains infinitely many primes; deleting primes<=324 leaves infinitely many. Ascending enumeration with finite trial primality and congruence tests therefore stops after finding22 primes in each of the finitely many unit classes. The union is the fixed finite catalogue H_cat and defines N_s exactly as before. This proves only termination of this catalogue; it gives no asserted effective largest-prime bound and does not establish the separate M0 index.

changes.old: Milne, Algebraic Number Theory v3.08 (19July2020), Theorem4.3 printed p.70 and Theorem5.1 printed p.85: every ideal class has an integral representative with norm at most (n!/n^n)(4/pi)^r2 sqrt(|disc K|); the unit group of a number field is finitely generated with rank r1+r2-1 and torsion its roots of unity. Exact PDF SHA256 de2066ee7a319c0e6e521895a7e9e9567c2804bcafc0c8e67c417e508f2bc26b; these are author course notes. For K0=Q(s), s^2=2, its integral basis1,s gives discriminant8 and two real places. Minkowski bound is sqrt2<2, so the representative has norm1 and every ideal class is trivial. Roots of unity in a real field are +/-1, hence the units modulo squares have order4. The sign vectors of -1 and epsilon=1+s are independent, so this sign map on the four squareclasses is bijective and a totally positive unit is a square. This supplies current344–346. It does not claim epsilon is a chosen fundamental unit.
changes.new: For K0=Q(s), s^2=2, the direct proof in ../qroot2-class-units-current/PROOF.md shows O_K0=Z[s] by trace/norm parity, and discriminant8. Nearest-integer rounding in both coefficients gives Euclidean remainder norm at most one half of the divisor norm, so every ideal is principal. Reducing a unit positive at the real embedding s>0 by powers of epsilon=1+s into [1,epsilon) forces its s coefficient to be zero; consequently all units are uniquely +/-epsilon^k. Thus units modulo squares have four classes, and the independent sign vectors of -1 and epsilon distinguish them. Every totally positive unit is a square. This replaces the general course-note Minkowski and unit-rank inputs only for this fixed field, and supplies current344–346. Rank, torsion, descent and saturation remain separate.

changes.old:
The ring of integers $\Z[s]$ has class number one because its Minkowski
bound is $\sqrt2<2$. It has four unit squareclasses. The sign vectors
of $-1,1+s$ are independent, so every totally positive unit is a square.
changes.new:
The ring of integers $\Z[s]$ is norm-Euclidean, hence has class number one.
Its units are $\{\pm(1+s)^k:k\in\Z\}$, so it has four unit squareclasses.
The sign vectors of $-1,1+s$ are independent, so every totally positive unit is a square.
